#+TITLE: Emacs literate configuration
#+STARTUP: overview
#+PROPERTY: header-args:emacs-lisp :tangle (let ((org-use-tag-inheritance t)) (if (member "INACTIVE" (org-get-tags)) "no" "~/.emacs.d/init.el")) :mkdirp yes

* About

** Usage

Every =emacs-lisp= block below is written, top to bottom, into a single =init.el= by =C-c C-v t= (org-babel-tangle). The order of the headings is therefore the load order. With that said, the header below must stay at top of file.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
;;; init.el --- generated from emacs.org, do not edit -*- lexical-binding: t -*-
#+end_src

** Tags

- =:BIND:=  The section defines some key binding.
- =:HOOK:=     The section installs some hook.
- =:ADVICE:=   The section installs some advice.
- =:FACE:=     The section modifies some face.
- =:MODE:=     The section activates *global* mode.
- =:DEFER:=    Part of the section only runs once a package is loaded.
- =:PERSONAL:= The content might need adapting per machine (paths, fonts).
- =:OTHER:=    The section is tangled to a different file than =init.el=.
- =:INACTIVE:= The section is not tangled.
- =:FIX:= The section implement /temporary/ tweaks due to my machine's build.

* Package management

** Gentoo =app-emacs/*=

I install these packages from Gentoo Emacs overlay. They are loaded by =/etc/emacs/site-start.el= and then =/usr/share/emacs/site-lisp/site-gentoo.el=.

| Package       | Used in         | Purpose                               |
|---------------+-----------------+---------------------------------------|
| vertico       | [[Minibuffer]]      | Vertical minibuffer completion        |
| consult       | [[Consult]]         | Search and navigation commands        |
| marginalia    | [[Minibuffer]]      | Annotations for completion candidates |
| orderless     | [[Matching style]]  | Match space-separated terms           |
| which-key     | [[Key hints]]       | Display available keybindings         |
| company       | [[In-buffer]]       | Completion popup while typing         |
| org-modern    | [[Looks]]           | Prettier Org buffers and agenda       |
| org-roam      | [[Roam]]            | Linked notes with backlinks           |
| calfw         | [[Calendar]]        | Month calendar fed by the agenda      |
| markdown-mode | [[Markdown]]        | Markdown                              |
| auctex        | [[AUCTeX]]          | LaTeX                                 |
| pdf-tools     | [[PDF viewing]]     | PDF viewer with SyncTeX               |
| magit         | [[Version control]] | Git interface                         |
| diff-hl       | [[Version control]] | Visualize diff in the fringe          |

** External programs

- =pandoc= :: Markdown preview and the conversion helpers.
- =dvisvgm= :: Org LaTeX preview in SVG.
- =dot= :: Compile dot figures.
- lilypond :: music sheets.
- plus the language servers used by [[Language servers]].

* Basic settings

** Startup :PERSONAL:

Homepage. Experimental.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(defun my/initial-buffer ()
  "Show org-file and a scratch elisp buffer by default."
  (let ((org (find-file-noselect "~/RoamNotes/inbox.org")))
    (delete-other-windows)
    (switch-to-buffer org)
    (set-window-buffer (split-window-below -12)
                       (get-scratch-buffer-create))
    org))

(setq inhibit-startup-message t
      initial-buffer-choice   "~/RoamNotes/inbox.org")
#+end_src

** Files :HOOK:

When you customize a variable inside emacs, the preference can be stored in [[info:emacs#Saving Customizations][a separate file]] (else emacs modifies your config file directly).

#+begin_src emacs-lisp

(load custom-file :no-error-if-file-is-missing)
#+end_src

Backups go into one directory instead of next to each file.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp

Symlinks into a version-controlled directory are followed without asking, which matters because most dotfiles are symlinks. Read-only files open in view mode.

*** Delete frame when done

Kill the frame when its title matches. This is useful for one-off GUI popup. See [[*Capture from the browser][Capture from the browser]].

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(defun my/del-temp-frame ()
  "Delete frame if its frame title matches."
  (when (equal (frame-parameter nil 'name) "emacs-temp-frame")
    (delete-frame)))
#+end_src

** Borders, mode line, and status line :FACE:HOOK:INACTIVE:

Borders, dividers and fringes melt into the background. The mode line is collapsed to a thin rule and the status moves up into the header line. The colours are read from the current theme, so the function runs again whenever a theme is enabled.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(defun my/apply-chrome (&rest _)
  (let ((bg     (face-background 'default))
        (subtle (face-background 'mode-line-inactive nil t))
        (rule   (face-foreground 'shadow nil t)))
    (dolist (f '(internal-border window-divider fringe
                 window-divider-first-pixel window-divider-last-pixel))
      (set-face-attribute f nil :background bg :foreground bg))
    ;; Mode line collapsed to a thin rule
    (dolist (f '(mode-line mode-line-inactive))
      (set-face-attribute f nil :height 0.1 :box nil :overline nil
                          :foreground bg :background bg :underline rule))
    ;; Status bar lives in the header line instead
    (set-face-attribute 'header-line nil :background subtle :box nil
                        :underline nil :inherit nil)))

(my/apply-chrome)
(add-hook 'enable-theme-functions #'my/apply-chrome)
#+end_src

The header line shows the buffer name, the major mode, and the position at the right edge.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(setq x-underline-at-descent-line t)
(setq-default mode-line-format ""
              header-line-format
              '(" " (:propertize "%b" face bold) "  (" mode-name ")"
                (:eval (propertize " " 'display '(space :align-to (- right 8))))
                "%l:%c"))
#+end_src

** Headings :FACE:DEFER:

Headings keep the default colour and are only one step heavier. In Org they also grow with their level.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(defface my-strong '((t :weight medium))
  "Structural text: default colour, one step heavier.")

(with-eval-after-load 'outline
  (dolist (n (number-sequence 1 8))
    (set-face-attribute (intern (format "outline-%d" n)) nil
                        :inherit 'my-strong :foreground 'unspecified)))

(with-eval-after-load 'markdown-mode
  (set-face-attribute 'markdown-header-face nil
                      :inherit 'my-strong :foreground 'unspecified :weight 'unspecified))

(with-eval-after-load 'org
  (cl-loop for (face . height) in '((org-level-1 . 1.4) (org-level-2 . 1.25)
                                    (org-level-3 . 1.15) (org-level-4 . 1.1))
           do (set-face-attribute face nil :height height)))
#+end_src

** Mixed pitch :FACE:HOOK:DEFER:

Prose buffers use the proportional font. Otherwise uses default (not necessarily monospace).

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(add-hook 'org-mode-hook      #'variable-pitch-mode)
(add-hook 'markdown-mode-hook #'variable-pitch-mode)
#+end_src

Define explicitly which faces should be fixed-pitch as needed.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(defun my/fixed-pitch-faces (&rest faces)
  "Make FACES inherit `fixed-pitch', keeping their existing inheritance."
  (dolist (face faces)
    (let ((old (face-attribute face :inherit nil)))
      (set-face-attribute
       face nil :inherit
       (cons 'fixed-pitch
             (remq 'fixed-pitch
                   (if (eq old 'unspecified) nil (ensure-list old))))))))

(with-eval-after-load 'org
  (my/fixed-pitch-faces
   'org-table 'org-formula 'org-code 'org-verbatim 'org-block
   'org-meta-line 'org-special-keyword 'org-property-value 'org-drawer
   'org-document-info-keyword 'org-date))

(with-eval-after-load 'markdown-mode
  (my/fixed-pitch-faces
   'markdown-code-face 'markdown-pre-face 'markdown-inline-code-face
   'markdown-table-face 'markdown-language-keyword-face
   'markdown-language-info-face))

(with-eval-after-load 'org-modern
  (my/fixed-pitch-faces 'org-modern-label))
#+end_src

* Completion

** Minibuffer style :MODE:

Vertico shows the candidates as a vertical list, Marginalia annotates them.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(setq vertico-resize t
      vertico-cycle  t)
(vertico-mode    1)
(marginalia-mode 1)
(which-key-mode 1)
#+end_src

** Matching style: Orderless

Orderless matches space-separated terms in any order. Vertico sorts matches by frequency. For example, to match =find-file= command,

- basic :: =fil fin= works. Space separated and each sub string must be correct.
- flex :: prefix =~fndfl= to use flex in current search.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(setq completion-styles               '(orderless basic)
      completion-category-defaults    nil
      completion-category-overrides   '((file (styles partial-completion)))
      completion-pcm-leading-wildcard t)
#+end_src

The built-in alternative, kept for reference.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp :tangle no
(setq completion-styles '(basic partial-completion emacs22 flex)
      minibuffer-visible-completions t
      completions-detailed t
      completions-group t
      completion-auto-select 'second-tab
      completion-eager-update t
      global-completion-preview-mode t)
#+end_src

(setq org-capture-templates
      '(("t" "Todo" entry (file "~/RoamNotes/inbox.org")
         "* TODO %?\n:PROPERTIES:\n:CREATED:  %U\n:END:" :empty-lines 1)
        ("n" "note" entry (file "~/RoamNotes/inbox.org")
         "* %?\n:PROPERTIES:\n:CREATED:  %U\n:END:" :empty-lines 1)
        ("l" "Todo from link" entry (file "~/RoamNotes/inbox.org")
         "* TODO %? (%a):PROPERTIES:\n:CREATED:  %U\n:END:" :empty-lines 1)
        ("w" "Quote selected text and link" entry (file "~/RoamNotes/inbox.org")
         "* [[%:link][%:description]]\n:PROPERTIES:\n:CREATED:  %U\n:END:\n#+begin_quote\n%i\n#+end_quote\n%?" :empty-lines 1)
        ("m" "Meeting" entry (file "~/RoamNotes/inbox.org")
         "* Meeting: %^{Topic} [%<%Y-%m-%d %a>] :meeting:\n:PROPERTIES:\n:CREATED:  %U\n:ATTENDEES: %^{With}\n:END:\n%?" :empty-lines 1 :clock-in t :clock-resume t)))

** Capture from the browser :HOOK:

=org-protocol= lets the browser hand a page (and the selected text) to =org-capture= through an =org-protocol://= URL.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(require 'org-protocol)

*** Desktop entry :OTHER:

This is the other half: the desktop entry that registers =emacsclient= as the handler for =org-protocol://= and names the frame.

#+begin_src conf-desktop :tangle ~/.local/share/applications/emacsclient-org-protocol.desktop :mkdirp yes
[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=Emacsclient (org-protocol)
Comment=Custom org-protocol handler (gentoo bug 950674, upstream bug 74467)
NoDisplay=true
Categories=Other;
Keywords=org-protocol;
Exec=/usr/bin/emacsclient -c -F "((name . \\"emacs-temp-frame\\"))" %u
Terminal=false
StartupWMClass=Emacs
MimeType=x-scheme-handler/org-protocol;
#+end_src

** Appointment notifications :HOOK:

=appt= reminds of today's timed agenda entries as desktop notifications. Entries without a time of day are skipped. Clicking a notification opens a new frame with today's agenda.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(require 'notifications)

(defun my/appt-agenda-frame ()
  "Open a new frame showing today's agenda."
  (select-frame-set-input-focus (make-frame))
  (let ((org-agenda-window-setup 'current-window))
    (org-agenda-list nil nil 'day)))

(defun my/appt-notify (min-to-app _now msg)
  ;; Appointments due at the same time arrive as lists.
  (when (listp msg)
    (setq min-to-app (car min-to-app)
          msg (string-join msg "\n")))
  (notifications-notify
   :title msg
   :body (if (equal min-to-app "0") "Now" (format "In %s min" min-to-app))
   :timeout (if (equal min-to-app "0") -1 900000)
   :actions '("default" "Show agenda")
   :on-action (lambda (_id _key) (my/appt-agenda-frame))))

(setq appt-display-format 'window
      appt-disp-window-function #'my/appt-notify
      appt-message-warning-time 15 ;; send notifications at 15 and 0 min
      appt-display-interval 15)
(appt-activate 1)
#+end_src

The appt list is a snapshot of today's agenda, so rebuild it after init (once =org-agenda-files= is set), whenever an Org file is saved, and just after midnight.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(defun my/org-refresh-appt ()
  (org-agenda-to-appt t)) ;; rebuild instead of append

(defun my/org-refresh-appt-on-save ()
  (when (derived-mode-p 'org-mode)
    (my/org-refresh-appt)))

(add-hook 'after-init-hook #'my/org-refresh-appt)
(add-hook 'after-save-hook #'my/org-refresh-appt-on-save)
(run-at-time "00:01" 86400 #'my/org-refresh-appt)
#+end_src

** PDF viewing :HOOK:DEFER:

Any file starting with =%PDF= opens in =pdf-view-mode=, as one continuous scroll instead of page by page.

SyncTeX backward search (click in the PDF, jump to the source). =pdf-sync-backward-search= hands this to =pop-to-buffer= as its action, and left unset it just splits the PDF's own frame. =reuse-window= with =reusable-frames= hands the jump to whatever frame already shows that source buffer; =pop-up-frame= only kicks in when no frame does.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(setq pdf-sync-backward-display-action
      '((display-buffer-reuse-window display-buffer-pop-up-frame)
        (reusable-frames . visible)
        (inhibit-same-window . t)))
#+end_src

** PDF in its own frame

Show the compiled PDF in a separate frame, instead of taking over the source window. =reuse-window= with =reusable-frames= picks up the frame from the previous compile, so re-running =C-c C-c= does not pile up frames.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(add-to-list 'display-buffer-alist
             '((derived-mode . pdf-view-mode)
               (display-buffer-reuse-window display-buffer-pop-up-frame)
               (reusable-frames . visible)
               (inhibit-same-window . t)
               (inhibit-switch-frame . t)
               (dedicated . t)))
#+end_src

** Remote :DEFER:PERSONAL:

TRAMP builds its own PATH from the list in =tramp-remote-path=. The earlier entries are checked first. The list can contain literal string paths and special variables, for example:

- =tramp-default-remote-path= : output of =getconf PATH= in remote.
- =tramp-own-remote-path= : output of =echo $PATH= in a remote login shell.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(with-eval-after-load 'tramp
  (dolist (d '("/usr/lib/llvm/21/bin"
               "/usr/lib/llvm/22/bin"
               tramp-own-remote-path))
    (add-to-list 'tramp-remote-path d)))
#+end_src

** Agent :BIND:

Copy a formatted prompt for the region or a function.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(defun my/copy-prompt-stub (beg end)
  "Format an agent prompt stub for the region or the defun at point."
  (interactive
   (if (use-region-p)
       (list (region-beginning) (region-end))
     (let ((b (bounds-of-thing-at-point 'defun)))
       (unless b (user-error "No region or defun at point"))
       (list (car b) (cdr b)))))
  (let* ((root (if-let ((p (project-current))) (project-root p) default-directory))
         (file (file-relative-name (or buffer-file-name (user-error "Buffer has no file")) root))
         (l1 (line-number-at-pos beg))
         (l2 (line-number-at-pos (if (and (> end beg) (= (char-before end) ?\n)) (1- end) end)))
         (lang (replace-regexp-in-string "\\(-ts\\)?-mode\\'" "" (symbol-name major-mode)))
         (text (format "@%s#L%d-%d\n```%s\n%s\n```\n"
                       file l1 l2 lang
                       (string-trim-right (buffer-substring-no-properties beg end)))))
    (kill-new text)
    (deactivate-mark)
    (message "Copied %s:%d-%d as prompt stub" file l1 l2)))

(keymap-global-set "C-c C-a" #'my/copy-prompt-stub)
#+end_src
